title: Optimal Lower Bounds for Online Multicalibration

An implication of this is that for any constant number of groups, the best rate for multicalibration is the same (up to constant factors depending on the number of groups) as it is for marginal calibration — and in particular, by the recent result of Dagan et al. The idea is extremely simple: if we have k k prediction independent binary groups, then before we make our prediction, we know which of the at most 2 k 2^{k} combinations of groups are active at each round t t before we must make our prediction. The sequence of rounds on which each combination of groups is active is by construction disjoint from every other. Thus we can instantiate a separate copy of any marginal calibration algorithm for each of the 2 k 2^{k} possible combinations of groups and run each on the corresponding subsequence. Naively this results in a blow-up in rates of 2 k 2^{k} . In this section we give a somewhat more refined bound that depends for each group on the number of distinct combinations of groups that it participates in, and further takes advantage of the convexity of calibration error upper bounds.
